reason: Mostly holds, with two parts that need fixing. HOLDS: (1) The GPU budget. Since the 04:55Z read of 20:29/30 h, 85b/85c/86a/86b/86c used ~2.1-2.3 h (dummy runtimes 1,721/1,736/1,460/1,357/~1,400 s), leaving ~7.2 h. That is ~15 K2 dummies, so the <=10 branch pushes fit with ~2 h left for E10. (2) The RA98 gate is an honest liveness check. Every cap/CI BASE dummy has the same readmits, 96/677/84/508 = 1,365 in run_stats.csv readmitted_nodes, and the READMIT 0.94 files have 168/1144/105/806 = 2,223. So 'per-clip readmitted <= BASE', 'nodes below BASE' and 'LOWREFINE below BASE' check that the knob is live and point the right way, whichever cap is BASE. (3) The T1 timing (RA98 PASS long before 50 lands, ~12:30-12:50Z) and T3/T4 fit W2b and the 23:30Z W4 freeze. REFUTED PART 1, the RUNTIME TRAP: the data do not support '+24% when parallel'. exp83a/exp83b were pushed together at 01:01Z (CONTEXT l.3344-3345), so their 1,798/1,882 s are parallel runs, not the 'solo' runs the finding cites. exp85a ran next to exp85b and took 1,388 s. exp86a/exp86b were pushed together at 06:36Z and took 1,460/1,357 s. The slow 85b/85c pair is ordinary run-to-run spread on the Tesla T4 dummy GPU: K2 dummies range 1,250-1,874 s, exp70q took 1,874 s with no CI, and the CI dummy exp75 took 2,288 s. So an amendment keyed to 'a logged concurrent lane' tests the wrong cause. A slow CI dummy can fail (6) with nothing running beside it, and a parallel one can pass. REFUTED PART 2, T2 is off-branch: JT+CI(b) is used only in W4 rows (a)/(b), i.e. under R+, and R is unknown until probe 50 lands (~12:30-12:50Z). Pushing it at the 48 read (~10:40Z) breaks the finding's own rule, 'push nothing that is not on the realized branch'. It wastes ~0.5 GPU-h with P~0.6-0.7 and gains nothing, because a push at T3 still passes by ~13:30Z, long before 23:30Z. Value: this is logistics only. It adds 0 on the LB by itself, and no new mechanism reaches R8.
fix: Log the push points and the gate lines with three edits. (a) Move JT+CI(BASE) (exp87a/b/c) from T2 to T3. Push it only when R+ AND (C+ or a testable C?). At T2 push nothing JT-related. (b) Replace the RUNTIME TRAP amendment with a noise-based rule, logged before any exp87 output is read: 'R22-A1 (6) v2: PASS if runtime <= 2,100 s. If 2,100 < runtime <= 2,500 s, re-run once and PASS if the re-run is <= 2,100 s OR runtime/parent-dummy runtime <= 1.15 (parent = the non-CI twin or the CI sibling, e.g. exp83a/exp83b). If runtime > 2,500 s, FAIL. Concurrency is logged but is not a criterion (evidence: 83a/b, 85a/b and 86a/b ran in parallel at 1,357-1,882 s; exp75 CI took 2,288 s).' (c) Keep the RA98 gate as written, but compare against BASE's per-clip readmits 96/677/84/508 (identical for exp70g/78a/78b/80a). Keep the RA92 gate as a soft expectation (nodes > JT(b), LOWREFINE > JT(b)), where a FAIL means only that dn <= 0. Everything else stays: T1 RA98 + exp84a under S3, T3 RA92 under R+, T4 exp87d/e under S3-up, T5 SEC only after exp81 reads '+'.
realistic_gain: 0 on the LB directly (logistics). The corrected rule saves ~0.5 GPU-h (the off-branch JT+CI push) and avoids both failure modes of the old runtime rule: a wrong-cause pass of a truly slow CI stack, and a spurious FAIL of a CI stack that is just noisy. That keeps the W4 CI/JT+CI files submittable by 23:30Z.
